findings.evidence: features/007-prune-skill/007-prune-skill-prd.md:R12 + AC-11 — R12 Stage 1 names byte-identical capture of the original entry plus post-write read-back of the archive entry's five fields. AC-11 verifies Stage 1's five-field check and Stage 2's per-surface mutation. The goal's Outcome names: 'Reversibility — every archived item retains enough context that a future user can paste it back into the live registry.' The reversibility property is the goal's load-bearing eval — `pruning is reversible (archive retained)` per `SKILLS.md` line 190. But walking R12's Stage 1 + Stage 2: the only verification is that the archive WRITE captured the original bytes. Nowhere in the PRD's R-set is there a contract that says 'a user pasting an archive block's `Original entry` content back into the source surface reproduces the source registry's pre-archive state byte-for-byte.' The byte-identical capture is the mechanism; the round-trip restoration is the contract that mechanism serves. AC-11 verifies the mechanism (Stage 1's byte-identical capture) but no AC verifies the round-trip property (the mechanism's value-creation surface). This is reverse-traceability: the AC verifies a sub-property; the goal-eval property is unstated as an R-level contract.
findings.claim: Orphan AC / unstated R-level contract — the round-trip restoration property (an archived item, restored from the archive file, reproduces the source registry's pre-archive state byte-for-byte) is the goal-eval contract but exists nowhere in the R-set as an explicit requirement. AC-11 verifies the byte-identical-capture mechanism but does not verify the restoration property the mechanism serves. A fresh agent implementing R12 might capture original bytes correctly AND produce an archive entry that is technically byte-identical at capture-time but where the surrounding archive block's escaping (e.g. fenced-code-block delimiters that swallow content if the original entry contained backticks) breaks the round-trip. The Stage-1 read-back as currently named would pass (the captured bytes are byte-identical) but a user pasting the archive block content back would NOT reproduce the source state. The contract is unstated.
findings.proposed_change: Promote round-trip restoration from a Stage-1 mechanism to an R-level contract. Either (a) split R12 into two requirements — R12 (byte-identical capture + post-write read-back, the mechanism) and a new R13 (round-trip restoration, the contract) explicitly stating: 'A user pasting a single archive block's `Original entry` content back into the source surface (re-inserting the rule into `rules/{tier}.md`, restoring the agent file from `admin/archive/agents/{YYYY-Q}/{name}.md` to `admin/agents/specialised/{name}.md` and re-adding the index entry, or unsetting the task-history `archived_at` field) MUST reproduce the source registry's pre-archive state byte-for-byte for that entry.' Add a corresponding AC verifying the restoration property — e.g. 'AC-12: For any archive block written by the skill, replacing the source-registry slice with the block's `Original entry` content produces a source registry whose pre-archive bytes for that entry are reproduced byte-for-byte (testable by capturing pre-archive bytes, running the prune, then running the restoration, and diffing).' OR (b) keep R12 as-is but add a sentence naming round-trip restoration as the R-level contract within R12 — phrasing that names it as a contract: 'The byte-identical capture at Stage 1 establishes the round-trip restoration property: a user pasting the archive block's Original entry content back into the source surface reproduces the source registry's pre-archive state byte-for-byte for that entry.' AC-11 then verifies the property by literal restoration test. Option (b) is the smaller surgical edit; option (a) is cleaner. Either closes the orphan-AC gap and lifts the goal-eval to an R-level contract.
